deduplication: Different mirrors, search snippets, arXiv/journal versions and author-hosted copies are grouped as one intellectual work. Search results from ResearchGate, Paperity, literature-review sites and spam pages were discovery-only and did not establish any conclusion. Only explicitly identified primary body readings support classifications.

entries.work: Nevo, OWR 17/2005, Rigidity and the lower bound theorem for doubly Cohen–Macaulay complexes
entries.body_read: PDF 36–37 / printed 960–961; Definition 1, cycle definition, Theorems 6–7 and Problem 8
entries.finding: Original target: fixed coefficient field; d-dimensional minimal-cycle pieces, d≥1, facet overlap and reorderability. Sphere strengthening is asked.

entries.body_read: Definition 3.1; Lemma 3.3; Theorem 3.4 and proof; Corollary 3.6; Problem 3.7 and following discussion
entries.finding: The sphere cover question is distinct from the additional CM-intersection route to Lefschetz. A no-sphere example defeats even the unordered cover, hence the original stronger decomposition.

entries.work: E. Swartz, g-elements, finite buildings and higher Cohen-Macaulay connectivity
entries.body_read: PDF 2 (ear definition), 12–14 (Theorem 4.1, definition, proof and Problem 4.2), 16 (Problem 4.8); relevant full-text terms scanned
entries.finding: Homology sphere explicitly has spherical homology globally and at every link. Theorem 4.1 is an ear-to-2-CM sufficiency result. Its extension to homology spheres/balls supplies tools; no earlier recorded full negative located in the inspected passages.
entries.version_auth: ArXiv primary submission history lists only v1, 2005-12-04 21:01:18 UTC.

entries.work: E. Babson and E. Nevo, Lefschetz Properties and Basic Constructions on Simplicial Spheres
entries.body_read: PDF 1–2: all-face-link homology-sphere definition and Theorem 1.2
entries.finding: Nevo himself uses the local all-face-link definition in the same g-conjecture setting. Join, connected sum and stellar subdivision preservation are results about sphere inputs, not a negative decomposition theorem.
entries.version_auth: Only v1 listed, 2008-02-07 20:35:07 UTC. The downloaded typeset PDF carries a later compilation date; chronology is pinned to arXiv history, not that compilation date. Attempted nonexistent v3 returned 404.

entries.work: C. A. Athanasiadis, Some combinatorial properties of flag simplicial pseudomanifolds and spheres
entries.body_read: PDF 1–5 (main results, definitions), full-text relevant-term locations including Theorem 1.3
entries.finding: Independent primary definition includes the empty face and all links. Flag 2-CM h-vector lower bounds do not supply a no-sphere 2-CM example.

entries.work: C. A. Athanasiadis and V. Welker, Buchsbaum* complexes
entries.body_read: v3 PDF 2, 4–7 (Walker criterion, CM/Buchsbaum* equivalence and counterexamples), 11–12 (Theorem 3.10/Corollary 3.11), rigidity/minimal-cycle discussion term-scanned; v1/v2 equivalent earlier propositions and Section 5 gluing statements compared
entries.finding: CM plus Buchsbaum* equals 2-CM. Counterexamples distinguish Buchsbaum notions and fail the relevant 2-CM hypotheses. Generalized gluing is sufficient for Buchsbaum*, not a recorded complete no-sphere example.
entries.version_auth: All three versions downloaded and hash-pinned. Numbering and gluing hypotheses change; no inspected version states a full answer to the original sphere question.

entries.work: R. Atanasov, Geometric two-dimensional duality groups
entries.body_read: PDF 1–3 / printed 69–71, definitions, Theorem 1.1, Bestvina Example 1.2
entries.finding: This aspherical-CM source uses a local CM convention. The example of two tori joined along an edge has nonzero H1 over Q and does not meet Nevo’s global CM hypothesis. No fixed-Q 2-CM assertion is recorded there.

entries.work: R. Woodroofe, Cubical Convex Ear Decompositions
entries.body_read: PDF 1–2, 4–7 (definitions, Theorem 2.3 and interval comment), 24 (Note 4.21), 31 (final questions); full-text relevant terms scanned
entries.finding: Builds ear decompositions for poset classes. The interval obstruction discussion cannot be reversed to obtain a 2-CM complex with no homology-sphere cover.
entries.dedup_note: The initial local download alias was schweig2009; title/author body verification corrected it to Woodroofe before the final ledger.

entries.body_read: Introduction, definitions, relevant full-text term scan; PDF 28–29 final remarks / Conjecture 9.1
entries.finding: Ear decompositions for selected poset classes and the 2-CM g-vector conjecture. The stated partial converse is numerical, not a sphere-cover theorem or counterexample.
entries.version_auth: ArXiv primary history lists only v1, 2006-05-09 19:22:14 UTC; later compilation date on retrieved PDF is not its submission date.

entries.work: J. Schweig, Convex-Ear Decompositions and the Flag h-Vector
entries.body_read: PDF 1–3, 13; Theorem 1.1, Definition 2.3, Proposition 6.6 and concluding obstruction
entries.finding: The counterexample blocks extension of a flag h-vector inequality to all CM/2-CM posets. It is not an obstruction to arbitrary local homology-sphere pieces.

entries.work: M. Larson and A. Stapledon, Complementary vectors of simplicial complexes
entries.date: Published online 2026-10-02; Forum Math. Sigma 14, e133
entries.body_read: PDF 1–5 context/main statements; 7–8 Examples 3.2/3.3; 9–11 examples/constructions including 4.9; relevant full-text sphere/decomposition/counterexample terms scanned
entries.finding: Graph examples refute algebraic extensions, while the 2-CM h-vector counterexample is explicitly a gluing of spheres and admits convex ears. Neither is a recorded negative answer to Nevo’s question.
entries.version_auth: Cambridge primary page and final PDF authenticate title, authors, DOI and 2026-10-02 date. Indexed author PDF link was 404; not counted as a separate work or a fully inspected earlier version.

entries.work: A. Björner, Let Δ be a Cohen-Macaulay complex
entries.body_read: PDF 4–6 CM/homotopy CM distinctions, 11 Theorem 4.4; full-text sphere/counterexample/decomposition terms scanned
entries.finding: Standard CM, Gorenstein* and homotopy distinctions; no inspected recorded no-sphere 2-CM conclusion. Non-shellable or non-homotopy-CM homology spheres remain spheres for this problem.

entries.work: A. Björner, M. Wachs and V. Welker, On Sequentially Cohen-Macaulay Complexes and Posets
entries.body_read: Introduction, Theorem 2.2 term locations, PDF 13–14 counterexample and Corollary 5.3; full-text relevant terms scanned
entries.finding: Wedge-of-spheres homotopy type and nonpure rank-selection counterexamples are different claims from embedded same-dimensional local homology-sphere covers.
entries.version_auth: Primary arXiv history lists only v1, 2007-02-26 15:53:18 UTC. Stale author link 404 was replaced by the primary arXiv version.

entries.work: C. A. Athanasiadis and M. Kallipoliti, Edgewise Cohen-Macaulay connectivity of partially ordered sets
entries.finding: Edgewise 2-CM is different from vertex 2-CM. The exhibited converse failures are not 2-CM and are not no-sphere-cover counterexamples.
entries.version_auth: Stale download failed; primary article metadata supplied migrated MSP PDF URL, successfully downloaded.

entries.work: N. Matsuoka and S. Murai, Uniformly Cohen–Macaulay simplicial complexes and almost Gorenstein* simplicial complexes
entries.body_read: Primary author-hosted PDF through web body: PDF 1–3 Theorems 1.1–1.2; 7–8 Proposition 2.8; 13–15 Proposition 3.9 and Examples 3.12/3.15/3.16
entries.finding: Uniform CM and almost Gorenstein* decompositions are weaker/different. The 6-vertex Example 3.12 is not 2-CM: deleting 6 leaves a disconnected link at 1, verified by a standalone finite face calculation.
entries.version_auth: Author publication list links the read PDF. Publisher and direct urllib PDF attempts returned 403; readable primary PDF body is preserved in raw web returns, not a downloaded binary. No exact arXiv version authenticated.
